HTTP OVER THE ONION NETWORK

Your server.
On Tor.

rotx serves static files and proxies HTTP services through your .onion addresses. Tor is embedded. Configuration stays in one file.

Get started Read the docs

Linux & Windows / amd64 & arm64

{ } rotx.conf 
http {
    compress zstd gzip brotli;

    server {
        name "<your-56-character-onion-name>";
        key_private keys/site.key;
        key_public  keys/site.pub;

        # Serve files from ./public
        root public;
        index index.html;

        # Forward requests to your application
        location /api/ {
            proxy_pass http://127.0.0.1:8080;
        }

        location ^~ /assets/ {
            cache 30d;
        }
    }
}
One server block per onion address.

Use your onion name and matching key files. Create public/ before starting.

RUNTIME Tor, built in
CONFIGURATION nginx-style syntax
IMPLEMENTATION Go + native Tor
SOURCE GPL-3.0

01 / WHAT IT DOES

Files, services, onion addresses.

Run several onion services in one process.
Give each its own keys, routes and settings.

root / alias

Serve your files

Static content with index files, MIME detection, byte ranges and conditional requests. File access stays within your configured root or alias.

proxy_pass

Keep your application

Forward requests to an HTTP or HTTPS upstream. Connections are reused, responses stream by default and buffering is opt-in.

server { }

Use multiple identities

Each onion address gets a server block. rotx validates the address and matching keys, then routes requests by their onion host.

zstd / gzip / brotli

Send fewer bytes

Negotiate compression, use precompressed files or cache generated static variants in memory or on disk. Enable proxy compression per route.

cache / header_set

Control the response

Set cache lifetimes and add, replace or remove headers. Policies inherit from HTTP to server to location, with explicit overrides.

pow / client_keys

Choose who can connect

Keep a service public or require Tor client authorization. Enable Tor's proof-of-work defenses for your onion services when needed.

02 / CONFIGURATION

Familiar syntax.
Explicit behavior.

Semicolons, server blocks and locations. A small set of directives, with validation before Tor starts.

01 Exact, prefix and regex routing.

02 Includes resolve relative to their file.

03 Errors include file, line and column.

Full configuration reference
Inside a server block
location = /health {
    return 200 "ok\n";
}

location ^~ /assets/ {
    alias assets;
    cache 30d;
}

location /api/ {
    proxy_pass http://127.0.0.1:8080;
}

Exact matches win. Otherwise, the longest prefix applies unless a regex matches. ^~ skips regex matching.

Inside a server block
server_tokens off;
header_set X-Content-Type-Options nosniff;

compress zstd gzip brotli;
compress_cache memory;

location /api/ {
    proxy_pass http://127.0.0.1:8080;
    proxy_compress on;
    cache off;
}

cache controls HTTP cache headers. compress_cache stores compressed static files. Upstream responses are not cached.

Excerpt from an http block
pow on;

server {
    # Add name, key_private and key_public
    client_keys keys/clients;
    server_tokens off;

    location / {
        proxy_pass http://127.0.0.1:9090;
    }
}

The directory must contain client .auth public keys. Clients keep their private keys. Authorization changes require a restart.

↳

A difference from nginx: proxy_pass keeps the entire request path. A base path is prepended; proxy_path replaces it.

03 / RUNNING ROTX

From config to onion service.

Download a release
  1. 1

    Get the binary

    Choose Linux or Windows, on amd64 or arm64. Tor and its native libraries are bundled.

    Binaries & checksums
  2. 2

    Add your configuration

    Put rotx.conf beside your binary. Supply your onion identity and keys, then set your files and upstreams.

    Complete example
  3. 3

    Start rotx

    Run from that directory. rotx validates the configuration, bootstraps Tor and registers your onion services.

    ./rotx Windows: .\rotx.exe

Running on Linux?

The supplied systemd setup runs rotx as an unprivileged user, with writes restricted to its data/ directory.

Service setup & permissions
With your binary, config and conf/ folder in place
$ bash conf/setup.sh

Registration is the first step. Descriptor publication and client reachability take additional time. Configuration changes require a restart.
